title: Pathological C-terminal phosphomimetic substitutions alter the mechanism of liquid-liquid phase separation of TDP-43 low complexity domain
authors: Haider R; Shipley B; Surewicz K; Hinczewski M; Surewicz WK
one_liner_zh: 该文研究TDP-43低复杂度结构域磷酸化模拟突变对液-液相分离的影响，虽用粗粒化模拟，但核心是蛋白自身相分离而非蛋白质-DNA互作，与本课题TF-DNA结合机制关联较弱。
abstract:
C-terminally phosphorylated TAR DNA-binding protein of 43 kDa (TDP-43) marks the proteinaceous inclusions that characterize a number of age-related neurodegenerative diseases, including amyotrophic lateral sclerosis, frontotemporal lobar degeneration and Alzheimer’s disease. TDP-43 phosphorylation at S403/S404, and especially at S409/S410, is in fact accepted as a biomarker of proteinopathy. These residues are located within the low complexity domain (LCD), which also drives the protein’s liquid-liquid phase separation (LLPS). The impact of phosphorylation at these LCD sites on phase separation of the protein is a topic of great interest, as these post-translational modifications and LLPS are both implicated in proteinopathies. Here, we employed a combination of experimental and simulation-based approaches to explore this question on a phosphomimetic model of the TDP-43 LCD. Our turbidity and fluorescence microscopy data show that Ser-to-Asp substitutions at residues S403, S404, S409 and S410 alter the LLPS behavior of TDP-43 LCD. In particular, in contrast to the unmodified protein, the phosphomimetic variants display a biphasic dependence on salt concentration. Through coarse-grained modeling, we find that this biphasic salt dependence is derived from an altered mechanism of phase separation, in which LLPS-driving short-range intermolecular hydrophobic interactions are modulated by long-range attractive electrostatic interactions. Overall, this in vitro and in silico study provides a physiochemical foundation for understanding the impact of pathologically-relevant C-terminal phosphorylation on the LLPS of the TDP-43 in a more complex cellular environment.

Statement of Significance

Proteinaceous inclusions composed of phosphorylated, C-terminal TDP-43 fragments have long been recognized as hallmarks of several neurodegenerative diseases, in particular amyotrophic lateral sclerosis and frontotemporal dementia. A rapidly growing number of studies indicate that these proteinopathies may be closely related to liquid-liquid phased separation (LLPS) of TDP-43, but the impact of phosphorylation on TDP-43 LLPS remains largely unexplored. In this study we used a combination of experimental methods and coarse-grained simulations to ascertain, in mechanistic terms, how phosphorylation at pathologically-critical C-terminal sites impacts liquid-liquid phase separation of the low complexity domain of TDP-43. Our results broaden our understanding of the mechanisms driving pathogenic process in these neurodegenerative diseases.
abstract_zh:
C末端磷酸化的43 kDa TAR DNA结合蛋白（TDP-43）标志着多种与年龄相关的神经退行性疾病中特征性的蛋白质内含物，包括肌萎缩侧索硬化、额颞叶变性及阿尔茨海默病。事实上，TDP-43在S403/S404位点，尤其是S409/S410位点的磷酸化，已被公认为蛋白质病（proteinopathy）的生物标志物。这些残基位于低复杂度结构域（LCD）内，该结构域也驱动蛋白质的液-液相分离（LLPS）。这些LCD位点的磷酸化对蛋白质相分离的影响是一个备受关注的话题，因为这些翻译后修饰和LLPS均与蛋白质病相关。在此，我们结合实验和基于模拟的方法，在TDP-43 LCD的磷酸化模拟模型上探讨了这一问题。我们的浊度和荧光显微镜数据显示，在S403、S404、S409和S410残基处进行Ser-to-Asp替换会改变TDP-43 LCD的LLPS行为。特别地，与未修饰的蛋白质相比，磷酸化模拟变体表现出对盐浓度的双相依赖性。通过粗粒化建模，我们发现这种双相盐依赖性源于相分离机制的改变，其中驱动LLPS的短程分子间疏水相互作用受到长程吸引性静电相互作用的调节。总体而言，这项体外和计算机模拟研究为理解病理相关的C末端磷酸化在更复杂细胞环境中对TDP-43 LLPS的影响提供了物理化学基础。

意义声明

由磷酸化C末端TDP-43片段组成的蛋白质内含物长期以来被认为是多种神经退行性疾病的标志，尤其是肌萎缩侧索硬化和额颞叶痴呆。越来越多的研究表明，这些蛋白质病可能与TDP-43的液-液相分离（LLPS）密切相关，但磷酸化对TDP-43 LLPS的影响在很大程度上仍未探索。在本研究中，我们结合实验方法和粗粒化模拟，从机制上确定了病理关键C末端位点的磷酸化如何影响TDP-43低复杂度结构域的液-液相分离。我们的结果拓宽了对这些神经退行性疾病致病过程驱动机制的理解。
